profiles.meeting_scenario: A coordination meeting between the RedSync systems workstream and the evaluation workstream as they prepare an internal milestone for refreshing the paper's large-scale results before a draft freeze. The systems side has a new sparse synchronization optimization for residual gradient compression that improved end-to-end throughput on their internal branch, and the evaluation side needs to rerun the official 128-GPU benchmark matrix and update shared tables for ImageNet and Penn Treebank. The agenda is to align on which code line the evaluator should use, what exactly will be delivered in Friday's handoff, how the 128-GPU rerun will be executed on the supercomputer, and what it means for the refreshed numbers to count as 'reproduced' for the draft. The expected outcome is apparent agreement that Arjun will benchmark the latest code after Lina's Friday package arrives and then refresh the result sheet, even though several second-order assumptions remain misaligned.

members.name: Lina Zhou
members.expertise: GPU communication kernels, NCCL tuning, gradient compression runtime optimization, cluster deployment
members.background: Lina is the main implementer of RedSync's communication path and usually develops on an 8-GPU DGX before promoting changes to the lab's 128-GPU supercomputer setup.
members.private_state: She wants the new optimization reflected in the draft quickly so the paper emphasizes practical speedup gains, but she knows the code is only clean in the systems repo and does not want to spend time packaging a full evaluation bundle.
hidden_assumptions: When people say 'the main branch' in RedSync coordination, they mean the RedSync repository's current main line, even if the benchmark suite still points to an older submodule revision.
A Friday 'package' means runnable code, a short launch note, and enough information for a technically competent evaluator to start jobs without extra packaging work from her.
If a 128-GPU result is 'reproduced,' the key thing is that the new sparse synchronization path recreates the expected throughput and scaling behavior of RedSync at cluster scale.
Running on the supercomputer normally implies the systems team's launcher defaults, including the NCCL environment variables and node-local staging that her optimization expects.

members.name: Arjun Mehta
members.expertise: distributed training benchmarks, reproducibility workflows, experiment tracking, paper-ready result aggregation
members.background: Arjun owns the benchmark matrix and final result tables for the paper, and he usually evaluates only frozen benchmark-suite revisions with pinned configs and the lab's standard Slurm-based execution pipeline.
members.private_state: He needs a clean benchmark refresh with minimal debugging risk because the draft freeze is close, and he wants anything entering the shared tables to come from the standard evaluation path so the comparisons remain defensible.
hidden_assumptions: When collaborators say 'the main branch' during a handoff, they mean the benchmark suite's main branch, which contains the approved launcher, parsers, and a stable RedSync submodule reference.
A Friday 'package' includes the exact run manifest needed by the evaluation pipeline: commit hash, pinned configs, environment modules, logging schema, and outputs that fit the shared parsers.

If a 128-GPU result is 'reproduced,' it must re-establish the expected convergence behavior and final accuracy/perplexity profile, not just the runtime speedup, so the compressed training result is safe to replace in the paper.
Running on the supercomputer normally means using the benchmark team's standard Slurm wrapper and logging hooks so new numbers stay directly comparable to prior tables.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree Arjun will run the update from the main branch.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: Lina means the current main branch of the RedSync systems repository, which contains her new sparse synchronization optimization but has not yet been propagated into the benchmark suite's pinned submodule.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: Arjun means the main branch of the benchmark suite, whose checked-in RedSync reference is an older stable revision that the evaluation pipeline already knows how to run.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both teams casually use 'main branch' as if there were only one obvious code line, and each defaults to the repository they personally treat as canonical, so the phrase sounds fully specific while actually pointing to different artifacts.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree Lina will send the 128-GPU package by Friday.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: Lina thinks the package includes the code update, a brief README with launch notes, and perhaps one smoke-test log showing the optimization runs.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: Arjun thinks the package includes a full evaluation-ready experiment bundle: exact commit hash, frozen configs for ImageNet and Penn Treebank, environment details, output field expectations, and anything needed for automatic ingestion into his benchmarking pipeline.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: In research coordination, 'package' is a familiar convenience term that often goes unexpanded because everyone assumes the other side knows the customary handoff format from prior collaboration.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree the draft only needs reproduced 128-GPU numbers this week.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: Lina thinks 'reproduced' means the 128-GPU rerun re-shows the expected end-to-end throughput improvement and scaling trend of RedSync versus dense synchronization, which is the practical systems claim she cares about.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: Arjun thinks 'reproduced' means the rerun confirms the compressed training still reaches the expected convergence behavior and task-quality endpoint, such as matching ImageNet top-1 accuracy trajectory or Penn Treebank perplexity within the benchmark team's accepted tolerance.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Because both throughput replication and training-quality replication are legitimately part of 'reproducing distributed training results,' the word carries a strong shared scientific tone that masks the fact that they are silently applying different acceptance tests.

misalignment_points.topic: How the 128-GPU run will actually be launched
misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree Arjun will run the 128-GPU experiment on the supercomputer once the update is ready.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: Lina assumes Arjun will use the systems team's launcher, including their NCCL environment settings, rank-to-node layout, and node-local temp staging that the sparse synchronization path was tuned and tested with.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: Arjun assumes he will use the evaluation pipeline's standard Slurm wrapper, module stack, hostfile generation, and logging hooks so the output remains comparable to prior benchmark tables.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: The meeting is about coordination of ownership and timing rather than execution mechanics, and both members believe they are referring to the obvious normal way to submit a 128-GPU job on the shared cluster.
